stdout_tail:
**Finding: No — logistic regression beats random forest here.** With scikit-learn defaults, stratified 5-fold CV ROC-AUC was 0.906 (LogReg) vs 0.891 (RF), a gap of ~0.016 in LogReg's favor. This held up under two independent stability checks (5×5 repeated CV with a different seed, and a fresh 70/30 held-out re-test split) — all three estimates agreed within 0.0003, and RF never beat LogReg on any of 25 repeated-CV folds. Likely explanation: default RF (unbounded tree depth) tends to overfit on this dataset relative to the well-preprocessed (scaled + one-hot encoded) linear model.

Outputs written: `analysis.py` and `result.json` in the working directory.

parsed_result.summary: No, with scikit-learn default hyperparameters, logistic regression achieves higher stratified 5-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC than random forest on this dataset (0.906 vs 0.891). The ~0.016 AUC gap in favor of logistic regression is small but very consistent across multiple validation checks.
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Dropped 52 exact duplicate rows. Dropped 'fnlwgt' (a census sampling weight, not an individual-level predictor). Numeric features (age, education-num, capital-gain, capital-loss, hours-per-week) median-imputed and standard-scaled; categorical features (workclass, education, marital-status, occupation, relationship, race, sex, native-country) missing values imputed with a constant 'Missing' category and one-hot encoded (unknown categories ignored) rather than row-deletion, to retain the ~7% of rows with missing workclass/occupation/native-country. Both models used pure scikit-learn defaults (RandomForestClassifier(), LogisticRegression()) except a fixed random_state=42 for the RF for reproducibility; no class-imbalance handling (e.g. class_weight) applied, matching the 'defaults' specification even though classes are imbalanced (~76%/24%). Metric: ROC-AUC via cross_val_score with scoring='roc_auc' on StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42).
parsed_result.verification_method: Two independent stability checks: (1) 5x repeated stratified 5-fold CV (25 folds total, seed=123, different from primary seed=42) with paired per-fold RF-minus-LogReg differences; (2) a held-out 70/30 train/re-test split (seed=999) not used in any CV fold, fitting both pipelines fresh on the 70% and scoring on the untouched 30%.
parsed_result.verification_result: Finding held up robustly. Repeated CV: LogReg mean AUC=0.9064 (std=0.0031) vs RF mean AUC=0.8907 (std=0.0039), diff=-0.0157, with RF beating LogReg on 0 of the 25 folds (95% range of paired diff: [-0.0193, -0.0107]). Held-out re-test split: LogReg=0.9079 vs RF=0.8920, diff=-0.0160. All three estimates (primary and both checks) agree to within 0.0003, so the conclusion that default LogReg outperforms default RF on this dataset is stable and not an artifact of a particular split or seed.
